title: Blueberry Sauce for Meats
excerpt: A sweet-and-sour, aromatic sauce, perfect for bringing out the flavor of your roasted meats. Made with the freshness and natural sweetness of our high-mountain blueberries.
imageAlt: Thick, deep purple blueberry sauce in a rustic ceramic sauce boat, served next to a roast pork loin and garnished with rosemary.
steps: In a small skillet or saucepan over medium heat, heat the olive oil and sauté the onion with the garlic for about 3 minutes, until tender and translucent.
Add the Fresh Pick blueberries, grated panela, balsamic vinegar and the sprig of fresh rosemary. Mix all the ingredients well to blend the flavors.

Cook over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring from time to time. You will see how the blueberries, carefully grown in the high mountains of Guasca, release their natural juices and characteristic sweetness as they soften.
With the help of a wooden spoon, gently press some of the blueberries against the side of the saucepan to release more pulp and get a rustic texture with delicious chunks.
Remove the rosemary sprig, season with a pinch of salt and black pepper to taste, and cook for 2 more minutes so the flavors concentrate.
Take the sauce off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes so it takes on a thicker, silkier consistency before serving it warm over your favorite cut of meat.
tips: This sweet-and-sour sauce is the ideal accompaniment for pork, turkey, chicken or even to give a gourmet touch to a good grilled beef tenderloin.
Thanks to the natural sweetness of 13° to 15° Brix of Fresh Pick blueberries, you won’t need to add excess sweeteners to get that perfect balance on your plate.
If you have leftover sauce, you can keep it in a sterilized glass jar in the fridge for up to a week. As it cools, its texture will become even more delicious.
